model_annotation: The chart presents grouped bar estimates of an “effect” measure across language families, with six model/condition series shown for each family and vertical error bars indicating variability/uncertainty around each bar height. The horizontal axis contains the categorical language-family groups (left to right: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic) and is labeled “family”; the vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with visible major tick labels at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (values extend slightly below 0 and up to the mid-30s). Within each family, six adjacent bars appear in a consistent legend-defined order and color: mBERT-L₂ (light cyan), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). Approximate bar heights by family are: IE-Baltic shows small positive values (about 2, 1, 3, 3–4, 5, and ~6, respectively); IE-Germanic shows moderate values for the L₂ series (~8 and ~10), near-zero to slightly negative values for the R₂ series (around 0 to −1), and larger B₂ values (both around ~15); IE-Indic shows near-zero L₂ values (around 0), larger R₂ values (~20 and ~18), and larger B₂ values (~24 and ~21), with comparatively tall error bars; IE-Romance shows mid-range L₂ and R₂ values (~6, ~4–5, ~5, and ~1) and B₂ values around ~12–13 (mBERT-B₂) and ~6 (XLM-B₂); IE-Slavic shows L₂ values near ~10–11 and ~9, R₂ values near ~0–1, and B₂ values around ~17 and ~15–16; IE-other shows L₂ values around ~6 for both, R₂ near ~0 with one slightly below 0, and B₂ near ~8 for both; Isolate shows all series clustered near zero to low positives (roughly 0 to ~2); Semitic shows L₂ values around ~11 and ~16, R₂ values below 0 (roughly −2 to −1), and B₂ values around ~15 and ~19–20, with notably large error bars on several series; and Uralic shows all series near ~0–1.5. The bars are not presented as sorted by magnitude (they follow the listed family order), and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent color-coding and the presence of error bars for each estimate.
